title: Countywide fraud risk assessment and hotline
summary: The county auditor reported signs of fraud, waste and abuse in emergency purchases during the pandemic and fire, and planned a countywide fraud risk review. The 2026 report found controls not designed well enough and no countywide policy for fraud complaints, and the auditor launched a fraud hotline.

timeline.text: The chair asked staff to send the report to boards and commissions that oversee departments that did not respond.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The auditor's office said the assessment cost about $200,000.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The report also found no countywide policy for handling fraud complaints.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The report found county controls are not designed well enough to address the fraud risks it identified.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: In the report's survey, 86% of elected officials saw medium fraud risk, but 95% of department heads saw low risk.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

timeline.text: The county auditor said a new fraud, waste, and abuse hotline is now live.
timeline.body: County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee
